thread:
acme_support: Hey team — multiple customers on trial report that credits are not being decremented after streaming reconnects. We have concrete examples where tokens were generated but ledger shows 0 debit. Started after upgrading to JS SDK v1.4.2.

acme_support: Example request:
```
request_id: abc123ts1719031000
session_id: sess-987
stream_events: chunk(1) -> disconnect -> reconnect -> chunk(2) -> complete
tokens_reported: 312
ledger_debit: 0
```

jess: Thanks, can you paste the request_ids and approximate timestamps for a couple of incidents? Also which streaming mode (SSE/WS) and is the client using idempotency keys or automatic retry? cc @dev-bob

acme_support: Using JS SDK v1.4.2 with SSE. Client sets idempotency key for non-stream completions but not for stream resume. One example above (abc123ts1719031000) — raw client log attached.

jess: Investigating. Do you see any 5xx responses before reconnect or socket-level errors?

acme_support: No 5xx. Socket drops after ~18s, client reconnects, resumes session id. Server responds with new chunks but final billing doesn't appear in ledger for that request_id.

dev-bob: This smells like a race where the streaming "finalize" event isn't emitted/consumed if the client reconnects before the server's finalization. If the finalize never lands on the consumer, ledger won't get a debit. Can you check if there's a session_finalize event for abc123?

acme_support: I queried event-store — for abc123 I see ingest/tokens events but no session_finalize event. Logs:
```
2026-01-12T14:03:20Z ingest: tokens=312 req=abc123ts1719031000 session=sess-987
2026-01-12T14:03:21Z socket: disconnect client=acme-js-1
2026-01-12T14:03:21Z socket: reconnect client=acme-js-1
2026-01-12T14:03:22Z stream: chunk processed req=abc123ts1719031000
```
ledger query returned no debit entry.

jess: Okay escalate to infra. @sre-oliver can you check the streaming-finalize consumer and Kafka window around 1719031000-1719031300? If consumer missed commits, that would explain it. We also need a plan to backfill ledger entries and prevent duplicates on manual retries.

sre-oliver: On it. Quick look shows transient Kafka consumer lag and a couple of commit failures in that window (1719031005 - 1719031280). That lines up with missing session_finalize events. I'll trigger a replay of the finalize topic for that range and run an idempotent reconciliation job to write ledger entries only if absent. Initial run estimate: ~12 trial accounts impacted. Will post a runbook and ETA.

finance-amy: If we need to backfill, product/billing needs a CSV with customer_id, request_id, tokens_to_apply, and timestamps. For trials we'll grant equivalent trial credits back (no negative billing). For paid customers we need to coordinate invoices or one-off charges — prefer to avoid surprise charges, so we'll discuss credits vs invoice adjustments.

jess: Thanks. @acme_support please DM the list of affected customer_ids + sample request_ids so we can prioritize. Also can you confirm if any customers saw the opposite (double debit) after manual retry?

acme_support: DMing list now. FYI a couple of customers reported double-debit when they retried the entire request (not resume) — probably because idempotency wasn't applied on the resumed path. So we likely have two related bugs: 1) missing finalize -> no debit, 2) non-idempotent resume/ retry -> duplicate debit. Happy to help test fixes.

dev-bob: Good catch. We'll add idempotency keys to the streaming-resume path and make ledger writes idempotent on request_id + idempotency_key. Also adding a small guard: if session_finalize missing but ingest tokens exist and session age > 30s, generate a synthetic finalize and enqueue. Tracking ticket: INF-4821.

jess: :thumbsup: I'll keep this thread open until the replay/backfill completes and the patch is deployed. Thanks everyone for quick turnaround.
